titleZh: 南澳大利亚州大型电池启用仪式
summaryEn: Musk speaks at the official activation of the world's largest lithium-ion battery, delivered ahead of his 100-day guarantee.
summaryZh: 马斯克在全球最大的锂离子电池正式启用仪式上发表讲话，该电池在他承诺的100天期限之前交付。

segments.textEn: Way to go. Everything with the vast majority of the world is still fossil fuel power. And this is really just the beginning. But I think what this serves as is a great example to the rest of the world of what can be done. So when this is done, which will be in just a few months, it'll be the largest battery insulation as measured by power by a factor of three in the world.
segments.textZh: 干得好。世界绝大部分地方的一切仍然由化石燃料供能。而这其实只是开始。但我认为，这为世界其他地方树立了一个很好的范例，展示了能够做到什么。所以等它完成时，也就是仅仅几个月后，它将成为全球按功率衡量规模达到其他设施3倍的最大电池绝缘装置。

segments.textEn: But there's still a long way to go. So we sort of need to do something about this.
segments.textZh: 但仍然有很长的路要走。所以我们有点需要对此采取行动。

segments.textEn: You sort of see the CO2 levels sort of bubble along and then it looks like a wall.
segments.textZh: 你可以看到二氧化碳水平有点起伏向前，然后它看起来就像一堵墙。

segments.textEn: So it's very important that we take action and take action now and really explain it matters. It matters whether we make the transition to sustainable energy in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years, it really is going to make a difference.
segments.textZh: 所以，我们采取行动、现在就采取行动，并真正解释这很重要，是非常重要的。我们是在5年、10年还是20年内完成向可持续能源的转型，这很重要，确实会产生影响。

segments.textEn: We're doing everything it can to accelerate it and by working with people like Jay and his team that really enable us, enables this to happen. And with your support.
segments.textZh: 我们正在尽其所能来加速这一进程，而通过与杰伊及其团队这样的人合作，他们确实让我们能够，让这件事得以实现。还有你们的支持。

segments.textEn: As you guys know, a year ago the situation was pretty dire.
segments.textZh: 正如你们所知，1年前的情况相当严峻。

segments.textEn: Yeah, first hand account that reason I was like, why is the place so dark? There's always electricity.
segments.textZh: 是的，亲身经历，那个原因我当时就在想，这地方为什么这么黑？一直都有电。

segments.textEn: Yeah. So now there will be.
segments.textZh: 是的。所以现在会有了。

segments.textEn: Anyway, so one tweet leads to another and pretty soon, pretty soon that.
segments.textZh: 不管怎样，所以一条推文引出另一条，很快，很快那个。

segments.textEn: So, yeah. So Mike, I saw this on Twitter. It's like, sure, Next day. By the way, can we do that?
segments.textZh: 所以，是的。所以迈克，我在Twitter上看到了这个。就像，当然，第二天。顺便问一下，我们能做到吗？

segments.textEn: Yeah, Exactly. Now it's 280, I guess like even more trouble.
segments.textZh: 是的，没错。现在是280，我猜麻烦甚至更大了。

segments.textEn: So it was only a couple months ago that we met and made the announcement for the deal. And a couple months ago none of this was here and it was just an announcement. But talk is cheap. Action is difficult.
segments.textZh: 就在几个月前，我们才见面并宣布了这笔交易。而几个月前，这里还什么都没有，那只是一项宣布。但空谈很容易。行动很困难。

segments.textEn: The reason we want to work as hard as we possibly could and get as much done as possible was to show that it's not just talk, it's reality.
segments.textZh: 我们之所以想尽可能努力工作、尽可能多地完成工作，是为了表明这不只是说说而已，这是现实。

segments.textEn: And in fact, everything that you see here, this whole event, everything is powered by those packs.
segments.textZh: 事实上，你们在这里看到的一切、整个活动、一切都由那些电池组供电。

segments.textEn: There are no generators. This is all literally energy coming from that system over there that used to be that dirt panel.
segments.textZh: 没有发电机。这一切用的确实都是来自那边那个系统的能源，那里以前是那块泥土地。

segments.textEn: You can sort of get a sense for the progress that was made over time.
segments.textZh: 你们大致可以感受到随着时间推移所取得的进展。

segments.textEn: There you go.
segments.textZh: 就是这样。

segments.textEn: Yeah, This is the actual power flow.
segments.textZh: 是的，这就是实际的电力流向。

segments.textEn: You can get this on your phone.
segments.textZh: 你可以在手机上获取这个。

segments.textEn: And so in a few months we'll be finished with the whole system and be delivering a 400 megawatts to South Australia.
segments.textZh: 所以几个月后，我们将完成整个系统，并向南澳大利亚州输送400兆瓦电力。

segments.textEn: So it feels like you wonder, well, how scalable, how scalable is the system? I mean, how much solar power do you really need to power Australia? And, and then how much battery pack space you need. It's actually remarkably tiny. Do you see that sort of that red square is that's the amount of solar area that you need power over square there.
segments.textZh: 所以感觉就像你会想，嗯，这个系统的可扩展性如何，可扩展性如何？我的意思是，为澳大利亚供电究竟需要多少太阳能？然后，然后你需要多少电池组空间。其实小得惊人。你们看到那个有点像红色方块的地方了吗，那就是你需要供电的太阳能区域，盖过那里的方块。

segments.textEn: It's about, that's about a tenth the area of Sydney. Just like, oh, Sydney's pretty big. But still that's. It's really, I think it's about 9 pixels on the map there.
segments.textZh: 大约，那大约是悉尼面积的十分之一。就像，哦，悉尼相当大。但仍然那是。其实，我想在那张地图上大约是9个像素。

segments.textEn: And we were going to put the size of the battery pack, but it's way smaller than one pixel. So it's only 7km square kilometers of battery.
segments.textZh: 我们原本打算标出电池组的大小，但它远小于1个像素。所以电池只有7公里平方公里。

segments.textEn: It will 100 days. Yeah, well, I mean, I mean think of this sort of like it's like satellites, the satellites, they're, you know, thousands of satellites going around Earth and they're all powered with batteries and solar, all of them. And there's some that have been up there for 20 or 30 years with zero maintenance. You can't send a repair person to go up and, you know, repair a satellite at 36,000 kilometers. So. So they're designed to just work for 20, 30 years with no maintenance.
segments.textZh: 它会100天。是的，嗯，我的意思是，我的意思是可以把这有点想成，就像卫星，那些卫星，它们，你知道，有数千颗卫星环绕地球运行，它们全都由电池和太阳能供电，全都是。而且有些已经在那里运行了20或30年，维护次数为零。你不可能派一个维修人员上去，在36,000公里处维修卫星。所以。所以它们被设计成无需维护就能运行20、30年。

segments.textEn: And really Earth, Earth is itself a satellite. It's a satellite in the sun. And so it's pretty obvious that if small satellites can be solar battery powered, the big ones can too. There's this game of loads of things, but I think people sometimes they're not quite sure, well, how big is it actually? And I just want to show it's really nice. It's like so small and very careful. And that is actually what the future will look like.
segments.textZh: 而实际上，地球，地球本身就是一颗卫星。它是太阳里的一颗卫星。所以很明显，如果小卫星能够由太阳能和电池供电，大的也可以。有这场很多事物的游戏，但我认为人们有时并不十分确定，嗯，它实际上有多大？而我只是想展示，它真的很好。它就像这么小，而且非常小心。而那实际上就是未来的样子。

segments.textEn: And the faster we get there, the better.
segments.textZh: 而且我们越快实现，越好。

segments.textEn: And there's really just. There's three parts to it. So collect the energy from the sun, store it because the sun doesn't shine at night, and then charge electric cars for transport and that's it.
segments.textZh: 而且实际上就只是。有3个部分。收集来自太阳的能量，把它储存起来，因为太阳晚上不照耀，然后给电动汽车充电以用于交通，就是这样。

segments.textEn: Well, thank you, thank you for coming. Thanks for driving so far. I hope you enjoy so very much. Appreciate your support. And it's because of the support of people like you they were able to actually get the stuff time. So thank you.
segments.textZh: 好，谢谢，谢谢你们前来。感谢你们开了这么远的车。我希望你们非常享受。感谢你们的支持。正是因为有像你们这样的人的支持，他们才能真正把这些东西时间弄好。所以谢谢。
